title: Flow node palette help in business words: the HTTP and approval node descriptions
body:
domain:spec#2 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibx5r5nhDMwpRs4SL6D

Filing gate: ③ Part 2 of #27838 (the producer half of #27356 row 15 and #27521 row 39). The `domain:spec` half lands in PR #28233 (the `approval.zod.ts` describes); the node descriptors are outside `domain:spec`, so the #27838 card thread carried this to the seat in its os-dev-report 6530217232 (`out_of_scope_findings`). ⛔ Not a claim. Triage sets the lane and grade.
Reach: every admin building a flow in Studio reads these as the palette and node-card text (observed on the 18.3.0 RC walkthrough).

## Observed (on `main`)

- `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/http-nodes.ts`, the HTTP node descriptor: the description and its config help name the outbox, retry / dead-letter, "HMAC-SHA256 secret → X-Objectstack-Signature", "a literal, read as written", "a CEL value envelope".
- `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-node.ts` ≈L138: "Route a record for human approval; suspends the flow until a decision, then continues down the approve / reject branch."

## Wanted (proposed wording from the card thread; the taker may improve it)

- HTTP description → "Send a request to an outside web service: wait for its answer, or hand it off to be delivered in the background with automatic retries."
- `method` → "The kind of request, such as GET or POST. GET by default; POST when the request is delivered in the background."
- `durable` → "Deliver the request in the background and keep retrying if it fails, instead of waiting for the answer; the flow does not see the response."
- `timeoutMs` → "How long to wait for an answer, in milliseconds."
- `signingSecret` → "A shared secret used to sign each request, so the receiving service can check it came from you (sent as the X-Objectstack-Signature header)."
- `body` → "What to send: a fixed value, or an expression worked out on each run."
- Approval node description → "Ask people to approve or reject a record. The flow waits for their decision, then continues down the approve or reject path."
- Same rule as PR #28233: business words in the first sentence, no ADR ids, internal field names or enum literals; engineer detail moves to code comments. Keep any hand translations in step.

Dedupe words: flow node palette description business words, http node descriptor help, approval node description.

Links back: #27838, PR #28233, #27356, #27521.
